meta.status: REVIEW DRAFT ONLY — no policy has been created, altered or applied in any database
meta.purpose: The POLICY layer over model/access_model.json. Policies are structured predicate objects, not SQL strings, so ONE definition feeds the SQL emitter, the runtime authorization evaluator and the linter. A second hand-maintained expectation table would be a second source of truth for authorization.
meta.defaultStance: DENY. RLS enabled with zero matching policies denies everything to everyone except the table owner and BYPASSRLS roles. A row appears below only where a named workload needs it.

principalMapping.note: access_model.json predates this vocabulary. The mapping is recorded so drift detection compares like with like rather than reporting a rename as a divergence.

findings.finding: the principal vocabulary in access_model.json (service, operator) predates WS12.2's (trusted_runtime, operator_context).
findings.resolution: recorded as meta.principalMapping so drift detection compares like with like rather than reporting a rename as a divergence. access_model.json is left unchanged: renaming it would invalidate 37 passing tests for no security gain.

findings.finding: migration_role was absent from access_model.json entirely, so the constraint 'the migration role must never be reachable from application runtime' had no principal to attach to.
findings.resolution: added to the RLS principal model with dbVerifiable true and NO policies, and the evaluator refuses it explicitly as a role-confusion attempt.

findings.finding: my first policy drafts granted anon SELECT on published prizes and authenticated SELECT on payments, allocations and prizes — MORE permissive than the ratified access model, which denies any anon or authenticated read of a table carrying a person's money.
findings.resolution: removed 4 over-permissive policies. Financial reads are served by views the runtime owns, which can project away external_reference and paid_amount in a way a row policy cannot. A draft that quietly grants more than the reviewed decision is the defect, not the review.

findings.finding: the access model declares trusted_runtime UPDATE on pool_fee_schedule, payment_allocations, prize_allocations and match_results; no policy implemented any of them.
findings.resolution: four UPDATE policies added. With RLS enabled, a declared access that no policy implements does not exist — the runtime would fail at runtime, not at review.

findings.finding: seven policies carried a rationale too short to review ("same as anon").
findings.resolution: rewritten to say what is exposed and why it is safe.

findings.finding: financialEntities was one list covering two different properties, so the harness asserted anon could read nothing financial — but pool_fee_schedule's CURRENT row is deliberately public, and the linter conversely failed to flag an anon read of payments because payments is not in sensitiveEntities.
findings.resolution: added financialNoAnonEntities (payments, allocations, prizes). A published price is not a person's money; a payment is. The same split already exists in access_model.json and should have been mirrored here.

anon.meaning: the unauthenticated browser holding the public anon key. Must be assumed hostile: the key is in the page source, so anything anon may do, anyone on the internet may do.

authenticated.meaning: a signed-in Supabase user. auth.uid() is verifiable in a policy. NOT currently used by the platform; modelled so the design does not need redoing when it is.

trusted_runtime.meaning: the server runtime (Edge Functions) using the service_role key. Bypasses RLS by design, which is exactly why every runtime path must be a narrow audited contract rather than a general-purpose door.

operator_context.meaning: an ARCHITECTURAL ABSTRACTION, not a database principal. R-GAP-1: there is no database-verifiable operator identity today. Every operator permission in this model is really 'trusted_runtime acting on behalf of an operator whose authority was checked outside the database'.

migration_role.meaning: the role that applies migrations. Has DDL authority and BYPASSRLS, and therefore must NEVER be reachable from application runtime. It is a principal in this model precisely so that constraint is stated and testable.

A_runtime_acts_for_operator.mechanism: the operator authenticates to the application; the runtime checks that authority and then acts with the service key, recording {operatorId, reason} in the audit event
A_runtime_acts_for_operator.weakness: the database cannot verify the operator; it verifies only the runtime. A compromised runtime is a compromised operator.
A_runtime_acts_for_operator.control: every operator-initiated contract records an operator id and a reason, so the audit trail attributes the act even though the database did not authenticate it

B_database_verifiable_operator.mechanism: operators become real auth.users with a claim or role membership a policy can test, so FUTURE_OPERATOR_IDENTITY cells become enforceable in RLS rather than in the runtime
B_database_verifiable_operator.prerequisite: adopt Supabase Auth for operators and decide whether a second approver is required for prize-affecting actions

policies.name: sync_state_trusted_runtime_select
policies.why: operational infrastructure. No anon or authenticated policy exists: a client has no use for a provider cursor, and its staleness is exposed through an operator health report instead.

policies.name: sync_state_trusted_runtime_insert
policies.why: the sync job creates its cursor

policies.name: sync_state_trusted_runtime_update
policies.why: the cursor advances on every successful run

policies.name: audit_chain_head_trusted_runtime_select
policies.why: the chain trigger reads the tail on every audit append; FORCE RLS binds the owner, so without this the append fails for a non-superuser owner

policies.name: audit_chain_head_trusted_runtime_update
policies.why: the same trigger advances the tail. No INSERT or DELETE policy exists for any principal: the single row is created by the migration and must never be added to or removed.

policies.name: audit_events_trusted_runtime_select
policies.why: investigations read the audit log through the runtime

policies.name: audit_events_trusted_runtime_insert
policies.why: APPEND ONLY. No UPDATE policy exists for ANY principal including the runtime: immutability is the property that makes the hash chain worth computing.

policies.name: audit_event_details_trusted_runtime_select
policies.why: the redactable payload sidecar

policies.name: audit_event_details_trusted_runtime_insert
policies.why: written with its parent event

policies.name: audit_event_details_trusted_runtime_update
policies.why: the ONE intentional UPDATE in the schema: erasure nulls the snapshots in place, which is why the sidecar exists at all — it lets erasure happen without breaking the chain.

policies.name: outbox_events_trusted_runtime_select
policies.why: the worker leases and completes events

policies.name: outbox_events_trusted_runtime_insert
policies.why: intent to notify is written with the business change in one transaction

policies.name: outbox_events_trusted_runtime_update
policies.why: status, attempt_count, lease and dead_at all advance through the state machine

policies.name: outbox_delivery_attempts_trusted_runtime_select

policies.name: outbox_delivery_attempts_trusted_runtime_insert

policies.name: pool_fee_schedule_trusted_runtime_update
policies.why: a superseded schedule row is CLOSED by setting effective_to, never deleted, so the entry that snapshotted it keeps its evidence

policies.name: payment_allocations_trusted_runtime_update
policies.why: reserved for an operator correction path only. The normal way to change an allocation is a COMPENSATING allocation, because an allocation records a decision and overwriting it destroys why the first one was made

policies.name: prize_allocations_trusted_runtime_update
policies.why: paying a declared prize sets paid_amount; the declaration itself is superseded rather than edited

policies.name: match_results_trusted_runtime_update
policies.why: superseding a result sets superseded_by_id on the OLD row. The old row's scores are never edited — that is what makes the correction history readable

policies.name: classification_snapshots_anon_select
policies.why: a league table is information the provider already publishes, and the app renders its G4/Z4/SA6 zones to every visitor. A predicate here would break the page while protecting nothing.

policies.name: classification_snapshots_authenticated_select
policies.why: identical to anon: a signed-in user must never see LESS than an anonymous one, and a league table holds nothing participant-specific to scope by.

policies.name: classification_snapshots_trusted_runtime_select
policies.why: the sync runtime and the scoring adapter read the authoritative snapshot.

policies.name: classification_snapshots_trusted_runtime_insert
policies.why: the sync runtime is the ONLY writer. This is the control that stops a browser establishing official standings: anon and authenticated have no INSERT at all, and standings decide zone boundaries and therefore scores.

policies.why: a league table is information the provider already publishes, and the app renders its G4/Z4/SA6 zones to every visitor. A predicate here would break the page while protecting nothing.

policies.name: competition_edition_standings_authenticated_select
policies.why: identical to anon: a signed-in user must never see LESS than an anonymous one, and a league table holds nothing participant-specific to scope by.

policies.name: competition_edition_standings_trusted_runtime_select

policies.name: request_idempotency_trusted_runtime_select
policies.why: the write boundary must read the record to decide replay versus conflict; no other principal may see it, because the stored response is a snapshot of a prior response and can carry whatever that response carried

policies.name: request_idempotency_trusted_runtime_insert
policies.why: INSERT ONLY: the record is written once, inside the business transaction. No UPDATE policy exists for any principal — a completed request record is a statement about something that already happened.

policies.name: participant_auth_links_authenticated_select
policies.why: KPLUS-F048. Every ownership predicate in this model is a subquery over this table, and PostgreSQL applies RLS to a table referenced inside another table's policy — measured, not assumed. Without this, that subquery returns nothing and every authenticated user loses access to their own participant, entries and predictions. Scoped to the caller's own links because a full read is an enumeration of the user base.

policies.name: participant_auth_links_trusted_runtime_select
policies.why: the runtime resolves ownership on every authenticated request and must see the whole link table to do it

policies.name: participant_auth_links_trusted_runtime_insert
policies.why: the runtime establishes the link when an auth identity first claims a participant

policies.name: participant_auth_links_trusted_runtime_update
policies.why: revoking or repairing a link is an update; the row is never deleted, so provenance survives

policies.name: migration_lineage_trusted_runtime_select
policies.why: reconciliation reads lineage to prove every target row has a source and every source element has a target; a check that cannot read what it checks is not a check

policies.name: migration_lineage_trusted_runtime_insert
policies.why: the backfill writes lineage in the same transaction as the row it describes, so a row and its provenance cannot become separated

policies.name: classification_predictions_authenticated_select
policies.why: a user reads only their own zone picks. Reading another's before the cutoff would let them copy a better player's G4/Z4 — the same FAIRNESS requirement that governs predictions, not merely privacy.

policies.name: classification_predictions_trusted_runtime_select
policies.why: scoring reads every zone pick

policies.name: classification_predictions_trusted_runtime_insert
policies.why: submission through the server, with the cutoff enforced against the SERVER clock

policies.name: classification_predictions_trusted_runtime_update
policies.why: an entrant may revise a zone pick until the cutoff
